_doc: Fable cold read, round 2, 20 leaves random-sampled (seed 20260904) from tough_leaves.txt. Page-fraction boxes [x0,y0,x1,y1], eyeballed ~0.01. Labels are one reader's judgement, NOT gold. New class codes used where the inventory has none — each is ALSO listed in the record as a proposal, never silently assumed: BT book/section title · HD display heading (dedication) · AN annotation body · LM lemma inside an annotation · IG interleaved gloss inside the verse column · GK lettered gloss key column · OR ornament (headpiece/tailpiece/woodcut) · RL printed rule · TB table (with TH header row, TC cell) · IX index/two-column entries · FN end-of-book marker · AT attestation/signatory block · MS manuscript pen marks (NOT type) · CR chapter running-head at outer head.

OT1-1609-P_0007.kind: PRELIM dedication epistle; ornament headpiece; display title; woodcut initial; no running head; dagger signature

regions.why: woodcut headpiece band, two rows of type-ornament; no text
'7' top right: pencil/ink foliation, not the printed page number — MS or PN, cannot tell at this scale
four-line display heading in diminishing caps, 'TO THE RIGHT / VVELBELOVED ENGLISH / READER…'; a dedication title, not a running head
woodcut factotum initial A, six lines deep
prose body of the epistle, two paragraphs, roman
right-margin summary 'The cause of delay in setting forth this English Bible.'
'VVhy & hovv it is allowed to haue holie Scriptures in vulgar tongues.'
repeated ink pen-strokes/ticks down the left margin — reader marks, NOT type; must not be OCR'd

OT1-1609-P_0025.kind: BOOK OPENING (Genesis 1); topical RH; ornament; book title; chapter head; argument; 8-line woodcut initial

regions.why: 'THE BOOKE OF / GENESIS, IN HEBREW / BERESITH.' three-line book title in caps
woodcut initial I, eight lines deep
left-margin italic citations 'Act. 14,15. 17,24. Psalm 32,6. 135,5. Eccli. 10,1. Heb. 11, 3. Iob 38. Ier. 10, 13.' — citation notes
long right-margin commentary note in two paragraphs (:: markers)

OT1-1609-P_0288.kind: ANNOTATIONS leaf (Leviticus); body is commentary in smaller type with italic lemmas; no scripture

regions.why: annotation prose continuing from previous leaf; small roman with italic citations inline; ends with a citation cluster
second annotation; opens with lemma '9. Svvete sauour.]' in italic — the lemma is the sub-region a reader anchors on
lemma '9. Svvete sauour.]' — quoted verse words + ']'
left-margin summary notes ×2 ('For benefites receiued: or desired.' 'Al sacrifices of the old Testament prefigured…')
'Not the external worke… External sacrifices were ordained: 1. to keepe the people from Idolatrie. 2. To induce them to internal vertues.'
'3. To signifie greater Mysteries of the new Testament.'
right-margin citations 'Io. 4. v. 24. Rom. 6. v. 19.' — citation notes, italic
'CHAP.' — catchword is the next page's heading word

OT1-1609-P_0344.kind: BOOK ARGUMENT (Numbers) — whole body italic; no running head text; chapter-reference column right

regions.why: 'THE ARGVMENT OF THE / BOOKE OF NVMERI.' two-line section title
book-level argument, ENTIRELY italic prose, ~50 lines — class is AR by content; a fount cue alone would agree, a position cue would call it MT
right-margin column of chapter/verse references keyed to the argument ('Epist. ad Paulin. qq. in Num. Exod.40 … 36.') — citation notes, many short lines

OT1-1609-P_1059.kind: BOOK BOUNDARY on one leaf: end of Judith annotations, ornament rule, then 'THE ARGVMENT OF THE BOOKE OF ESTHER'

regions.why: closing annotation prose of Judith, small type with inline italic refs
right summary 'Manie incitements concurring to the contrarie made her widowhood more excellent.'
type-ornament rule separating the two books
'THE ARGVMENT OF THE / BOOKE OF ESTHER.'
book argument, italic/roman mixed prose, two paragraphs
left citations 'Melito S. Atha. S. Greg. Nazian. Origen apud Euseb. lib 6. c. 25. hist.'

OT1-1609-P_1134.kind: BOOK ARGUMENT continuation (Job), italic+roman mixed; left summaries only; physical crease bottom-left

regions.why: book-argument prose in five paragraphs, italic summary phrases alternating with roman narrative — one text

OT2-1610-P_0008.kind: PRELIM 'PROEMIAL ANNOTATIONS' prose; left summaries; right citation column

regions.why: annotation prose, two paragraphs, roman with italic quotations and refs — this IS the body of the leaf
'The common voice of Christians & some general councels, cal it Dauids Psalter.'
'S Ierom attributeth the summe of this booke to Dauid only.'
right citation column 'Mat. 22. v.16. Act. 4. v.24. Ro. 4. v.6. Ro. 11. v.9. Heb. 4. v.7.'

OT2-1610-P_0022.kind: PSALTER INTERLEAVED: annotation tail, psalm head, argument, title verse, verses with INTERLEAVED italic glosses keyed by letter to a LEFT gloss column

regions.why: tail of annotations for Psalm 2, small type, lemma '11. Reioyce vvith trembling.]'
'PSALME. III.' — the psalm head is the chapter head of this book
italic psalm argument, four lines, ends 'Resurrection.'
'Dauid persecuted by his sonne. The 8. key.' — beside the argument
title verse '† The Psalme of Dauid, when he fled…' with VN 1
Ps 3:2-9 verse text, roman — BUT italic gloss lines are set BETWEEN the roman verse lines inside this same measure

the interleaved italic glosses ('haue sinned. b that al Israel (1.Reg.15.v.13.) with al their Absolom…') — same measure as MT, different fount, keyed by superscript letters; a NEW class, cannot be MN (not in the margin) and must not be MT

LEFT column of lettered glosses 'a O God let me know… c my life d he can not escape… h heauen. i I lay downe…' — a gloss KEY column, letter-keyed to the body; sub-kind of MN but structurally a column, not notes

OT2-1610-P_0023.kind: ANNOTATIONS section with its own header 'ANNOTATIONS. PSALME. III.'; then next psalm head + argument

regions.why: 'ANNOTATIONS. PSALME. III.' — a section header for the annotation block; reads as heading, sits like one; sub-kind of CH ('annotation head')
annotation prose in four lemma-led paragraphs ('1. Psalme of Dauid.]', '1. VVhen he fled…]', '6. I haue slept…]')
'Titles of the Psalmes added by Esdras and the Septuagint.'
'Fiue thinges to be noted in the titles.'
'VVhy this is called the Psalme of Dauid.'
'The time and occasion of making this Psalme.'
'The same Scripture hath diuers literal senses.'
italic psalm argument 'The holie prophet teacheth…'
'Confidence in God necessary The 7. key.' beside the argument

OT2-1610-P_0024.kind: PSALTER INTERLEAVED, full page of verses with lettered glosses; 'VV' two-letter initial; annotation header + start at foot

regions.why: title verse 'Vnto the end, in songues, the Psalme of Dauid.' with gloss line and VN 1
'VV' two-line initial set as two V sorts — a drop capital made of two letters
interleaved italic gloss lines between verses, letter-keyed (d being straictly beseeged… g honour, and transitorie glorie…)
left lettered gloss key column a..z, full height, italic
first annotation, lemma '1. Vnto the end.)'

OT2-1610-P_0025.kind: ANNOTATIONS-ONLY leaf, dense small type, right-margin summary column, left citations

regions.why: annotation prose, whole leaf, lemma '6. Sacrifice of Iustice.]' at y≈0.28
'To the end in the titles of Psalmes.'
'Three spiritual sacrifices necessarie.' 'Of penance, Iustice, Praise.'
column of nine short summaries 'VVhat is due to God.' … 'Light of reason sheweth there is a God that rewardeth.'

OT2-1610-P_0670.kind: BOOK OPENING (Baruch); no running head; ornament + rules; book title; ch head; argument; asterisk alternate-reading note

regions.why: type-ornament band between two printed rules
'The whole time of taking Ierusalem…' long left note
'* or, manah sacrifice.' — an ALTERNATE-READING note keyed by asterisk; sub-kind of MN (variant), not commentary

OT2-1610-P_0747.kind: scripture chapter break with right notes (standard)

regions.why: ':: This frequent phrase here and in other places signifieth, turne thy speach to speake of such and such people…'
':: God accounteth al iniuries done against his Church, as done against himself…'

OT2-1610-P_1085.kind: END OF BOOK (4 Esdras) — verses end, 'FINIS.' centred, lower page BLANK; no signature/catchword

regions.why: 'FINIS.' centred — end-of-book marker; not a heading, not a catchword; NO class in inventory
BLANK lower page — must be reported as blank, not searched for a catchword

OT2-1610-P_1089.kind: RULED CHRONOLOGICAL TABLE ('OF THE OLD TESTAMENT') — five columns with header row, vertical rules, a centred section title mid-page; NOT a text column

regions.why: TABLE HEADER ROW: 'Anni mundi. | Patriarches. | The sacred Historie. | Schismes and infidelitie. | Scriptures.' between double rules
TABLE BODY, upper: 5 columns separated by vertical rules; cells hold dates ('x 1656.'), names, narrative prose, and refs
'THE END OF THE FIRST AGE, / AND BEGINNING OF THE SECOND.' centred display line spanning the table — a section title inside the table
TABLE BODY, lower: same five columns; left column of lettered dates 'y 1658. z 1693. a 1723. b 1753…', names column, narrative, and a right italic note cell
'* Not affirming but supposing that Cainan was the sonne of Arphaxad…' italic asterisk note — set in the rightmost table column but it is a note
printed rules: two horizontal doubles at header, one at the section title, four vertical column rules — geometry a reader uses to find cells

OT2-1610-P_1112.kind: INDEX 'A PARTICVLAR TABLE' — TWO EQUAL COLUMNS of alphabetical entries with page refs; no notes, no verses

regions.why: LEFT index column, entries 'Ægypt… Affinitie… Agar… Aggeus… Ahias… Alcimus… Alleluia… Alexander… Almes deedes… Alphabet… Altares… Aman' each with italic a./b. volume letters and page numbers
RIGHT index column 'Ambition… Amos… Amram… Angels… Antichrist… Antiochus… Antiquitie'
the inter-column gutter — a reader uses it to split; there is no rule, just white; no class

OT2-1610-P_1136.kind: LATIN APPROBATION (Censura) — italic title, Latin prose in an irregular/worn face, three signatory lines, lower 40% blank

regions.why: 'Censura trium Theologorum Anglorum, extra collegium commorantium' two italic display lines — a document title
Latin prose, 16 lines — the approbation text; type is irregular/blotted (worn or possibly a facsimile leaf) — READING confirms it is print, not manuscript
three signatory entries: caps NAME + italic title ('JOANNES WRIGHTVS, Ecclesiæ collegiatæ Gloriosæ Virginis, Certracensis Decanus' etc.) — an ATTESTATION block, NO class in inventory
BLANK lower 40% of the leaf — reported as blank

NT-1582-B_0028.kind: PRELIM PREFACE END — prose with inline GREEK, left summaries, right citations, large woodcut TAILPIECE, lower third blank; no catchword or signature

regions.why: preface prose, five paragraphs, roman with italic Latin and inline Greek (ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου…) — Greek inside the body is a fount switch, not a region
'In the beginning of bookes, Matthew, Paul &c. not S. Matthew. S. Paul &c.'
'The margent reading sometime preferred before the text.'
woodcut TAILPIECE, centred below the last line — ornament, no text

NT-1582-B_0562.kind: NT SETTING (Rhemes): annotations ABOVE a rule, then chapter head + argument + 7-line woodcut initial + verses; THREE-part head with 'CHA. III.' at outer; Greek in right margin; frame rule at right edge

regions.why: 'CHA. III.' — CHAPTER RUNNING-HEAD at the outer head; NT setting puts the chapter number in the headline, not a topical title — distinct from RH by content
annotations for ch.2 in small type, five lemma-led paragraphs ('10. Name of IESVS.]' '12. With feare and trembling.]' '13. Worketh in you.]' '17. The sacrifice.]')
left summaries ×5 ('The Protestants vvill haue no reuerence done at the name of IESVS.' … 'Martyrdom.')
printed rule separating annotations from the next chapter
woodcut initial F, seven lines deep
'c By allusion of vvords, he calleth the carnal Christian Iews that yet boasted in the circumcision…' left note keyed by letter
GREEK words 'κατατομή περιτομή' in the right margin — a note in Greek; class MN, fount Greek
vertical frame rule at the right edge of the text area

NT-1582-B_0564.kind: NT SETTING: ANNOTATIONS fill 70% (no scripture on this leaf), rule, chapter head + argument, then page ENDS — catchword only

regions.why: annotations for ch.3 in small type, lemmas '12. Not that novv.]' '15. Othervvise minded.]'
left summaries ×6 ('Double perfection…' 'The heretikes folish defense…' 'The difference betvvene the disagreing of auncient fathers…' 'The spiteful vvritings…' 'A notable place of S. Augustine.')
'Therefore' — catchword with NO body text above it on this leaf; the chapter text begins overleaf
